slope/line: A straight line climbs at the same rate everywhere. Each time x steps by one, two x plus one rises by two, so its slope is two.
slope/shift: The plus one only sets the height: two x minus two sits lower but tilts the same way, slope two. The constant never changes the slope.
slope/fall: A line that falls has a negative slope. Minus three x plus four drops three for every step: slope minus three.
slope/forms: However the line is written, find the number multiplying x. Three times, x minus one, is three x minus three: slope three. Half of two x plus four is x plus two: slope one.
slope/curve: A curve is steeper in some places than others. Take f of x equals x squared, where f of x is the value f gives for the input x. How steep is it at x equals one?
slope/two: Pick a second point a step h to the right, at x equals two. Between them, f goes from one to four.
slope/rise: The rise is the later value minus the earlier one: four minus one, three. Over a run of one, the slope between the two points is three.
slope/formula: Written out: the slope between x and x plus h is f of x plus h, minus f of x, all over h.
shrink/shrink: Shrink the step to a half. f of one point five is two point two five, so the rise is two point two five minus one: one point two five. Over a run of zero point five, the slope is one point two five over zero point five: two point five.
shrink/tenth: With a step of a tenth, f of one point one is one point two one: a rise of zero point two one over a run of zero point one, a slope of two point one.
shrink/limit: As h shrinks toward zero, the slope settles on two: two point zero one, then two point zero zero one. That limit is the derivative of f at one, written with a tick read “prime”: f prime of one equals two.
shrink/tangent: The line with that slope just grazes the curve at x equals one. It is the tangent.
shrink/line: A straight line has the same slope over every step, so for f of x equals two x plus one, the derivative is two at every x: f prime of x equals two.
